items.title: Second Regional Review Conference on Implementation of the Forest Rights Act Held in Kolkata
items.summary: The Conference brought together senior functionaries of the Tribal Welfare, Revenue and Forest Departments and Tribal Research Institutes of eight States, namely West Bengal, Assam, Tripura, Jharkhand, Odisha, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh.

facts.text: The Conference follows the First Regional Review Conference held in Bengaluru on 10 September 2026 for the Southern States.
In his Keynote Address, the Joint Secretary said that as on 31 st August 2026, over 54 lakh claims had been received nationally, and about 25 lakh titles had been distributed.
About 11 lakh claims still remain pending at different stages, while over 18 lakh claims have been rejected.

Her presentation also covered the importance of incorporating the Record of Forest Rights into revenue and forest records in line with the Ministry’s advisory of 24 June 2026 and Habitat Rights under the Ministry’s guidelines of 5 January 2026.

bullets: ABS means commercial benefits from bioresources are shared with the communities that provide them. It covers plant, animal and microbial resources and traditional knowledge, but excludes human genetic material. The CBD introduced it in 1992 and the Nagoya Protocol put it into operation in 2010.

Kani model : the Kani tribe of Kerala shared knowledge of Arogyapacha (Trichopus zeylanicus). TBGRI, Thiruvananthapuram, used it to develop the anti-fatigue drug "Jeevani" and shared the licence fee and royalty with a Kani trust. It was the first well-known benefit-sharing model.
NBA's ABS has raised over ₹266 crore since 2008. Red Sanders accounts for 45% (₹120 crore) of that and the seed sector for 32.3% (LENSD, 26 Jun 2026).

New fund rules (NBA): if a resource comes from an identifiable repository, 25-40% of ABS funds go to it and 60-75% go to local communities through SBBs/UTBCs. If the origin cannot be traced, the money goes to conservation (VIS Apr 2026). India also notified ABS Regulations 2025, which cover Digital Sequence Information (APPCA).

APSBB plans a first-of-its-kind Marine ABS framework for fishermen and will strengthen about 13,000 BMCs (TH, 30 Apr 2026). NBA sanctioned ₹82 lakh to APSBB for Red Sanders conservation (LENS Oct 2025).

bullets: Also called reserve money, monetary base, base money, central bank money; basis of credit creation; the most important money indicator for RBI.
As the PYQ frames it: H = currency held by the public + cash reserves of commercial banks (with themselves and with RBI) + other deposits with RBI.

bullets: El Nino: central/east equatorial Pacific at least 0.5°C warmer for five consecutive overlapping 3-month periods; 6 of 10 El Nino years give weak Indian monsoons (TH, 1 Feb 2026).
La Nina generally strengthens the monsoon, brings colder winters and more Bay cyclones (VIS 2026).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 4 Geography › D-1 › Ocean-atmosphere interaction - El Nino, La Nina, ENSO, Indian Ocean Dipole, Walker circulation › El Nino - where the SST anomaly forms, Peru current, recurrence, impacts
bullets: El Nino = abnormal warming of the central and eastern equatorial Pacific; an unusual warm current flows southwards along the Peru (west South American) coast, replacing the cold Peruvian (Humboldt) current. It flows in the Pacific Ocean.
Mechanism: easterly trade winds weaken or reverse; warm water piled in the western Pacific shifts east; the warming weakens winds further (Bjerknes feedback).
Rising air shifts east, air descends over the Indian Ocean - high pressure there, delayed/weak Indian monsoon, drought; lower summer-crop (rice, sugarcane) yields, food inflation, harsher heat.
Historically 6 of 10 El Nino years brought depressed Indian rainfall; the last global El Nino was 2023-24 (TH, 1 Feb 2026).
Exam angle: El Nino is a climate pattern, not a storm; statement sets on Peru warm current, 3-7-year recurrence and meaning of the name.

bullets: Art. 329(a): laws on delimitation and allotment of seats cannot be questioned in court; Art. 329(b): an election can be challenged only by an election petition .
